# OmniForge Materials — The Batch That Lost Its Passport
> **GitHub-first narrative edition · GICS02 · 2026-10-19.** This enterprise is fictional. GitHub is canonical; Notion is the knowledge-management hub. Names, incidents and strategic options below are illustrative teaching additions. Original research and 13 HR child-page links are preserved below. Daily reconciliation configuration and manual transfers do not establish successful unattended integration.
**Start here:** [Executive One-Pager](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/02-materials/omniforge-materials-ltd/executive-one-pager.md) · [Hero Story](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/02-materials/omniforge-materials-ltd/hero-story.md) · [22-Section Master](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/02-materials/omniforge-materials-ltd/master/README.md) · [16 Fictional Personas](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/02-materials/omniforge-materials-ltd/personas/persona-cards.md) · [12 Simulations](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/02-materials/omniforge-materials-ltd/simulations/README.md) · [Seven Derived Streams](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/02-materials/omniforge-materials-ltd/derived-streams/README.md) · [Resources](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/02-materials/omniforge-materials-ltd/resources/README.md)
## Prologue — A shipment with three versions of the truth
A fictional industrial customer queries a shipped batch's certificate after a laboratory correction fails to reach the customer portal. At a plant, a critical-asset warning arrives while procurement cannot reconcile a recycled-feedstock record. These invented events expose a discovery question: can OmniForge trust its material, quality and carbon evidence from extraction through recovery?
## Act I — Understand the Enterprise (OMF-M01–04)
Fictional CEO **Ananya Deshpande (OMF-P01)** leads a USD42 B materials enterprise with 46,000 employees across 31 countries, headquartered in Mumbai and Rotterdam. Its revenue mix is steel/alloys 30%, cement/aggregates 22%, chemicals 20%, mining/minerals 16% and advanced materials 12%.
The source lists 54 production sites,27 mines/quarries and 18 cement plants; these counts may overlap. Fragmented planning, inconsistent master data,180+applications and isolated operational data make reliable decisions difficult.
**Discovery challenge:** Which broken handoff creates the greatest customer, safety or value risk?
[Read the Enterprise theme](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/02-materials/omniforge-materials-ltd/master/theme-a-enterprise.md)
## Act II — Choose the Future (OMF-M05–08)
CFO **Thomas van Dijk (OMF-P02)** demands financial discipline. COO **Kavita Rao (OMF-P03)** protects operational continuity. Chief Digital and Sustainability Officer **Sofia de Vries (OMF-P04)** requires auditable material and carbon evidence.
Compare three illustrative options: local pilots, enterprise platform first, and federated value-stream pilots under common safety/data standards. The third is provisional and must survive evidence gates.
The source's 35%Scope 1/2 emissions reduction by 2032 differs from a Year 3 carbon-intensity index 100→75. Both remain targets with distinct boundaries.
[Read the Strategy theme](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/02-materials/omniforge-materials-ltd/master/theme-b-strategy.md)
## Act III — Architect the Digital Thread (OMF-M09–12)
The source value chain is **Explore → Extract → Process → Manufacture → Distribute → Recover → Reuse**. Illustrative transformation streams connect Feedstock-to-Qualified-Material, Asset-to-Reliability, Order-to-Trusted-Delivery, Recover-to-Reuse and Evidence-to-Carbon-Claim.
Architect **Priya Nair (OMF-P13)** connects capabilities and process owners to ERP, MES, EAM, LIMS, MDM, edge, APIs and events. Quality lead **Rohan Kulkarni (OMF-P08)** demands traceable lab corrections and batch genealogy. Data/AI lead **Diego Alvarez (OMF-P14)** requires ownership and lineage; CISO **Hassan Al-Farsi (OMF-P12)** insists critical controls remain within safe plant boundaries.
[Read the Architecture theme](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/02-materials/omniforge-materials-ltd/master/theme-c-architecture.md)
## Act IV — Fund Learning Before Scale (OMF-M13–16)
The fictional source proposes **USD540 M over 36 months**: operations/OT230 M, data/AI125 M, supply-chain/CX90 M, cyber 55 M and change 40 M.
Listed benefit categories total **USD350 M**, but 65 M working capital may represent cash release rather than recurring savings. Predictive-maintenance 70 M may overlap efficiency 190 M. No validated NPV or payback is provided.
Year 1 establishes foundations and pilots; Year 2 integrates data/AI/planning; Year 3 extends twins, circularity and controlled optimization. Safety, quality, workforce and financial gates govern scale.
[Read the Transformation theme](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/02-materials/omniforge-materials-ltd/master/theme-d-transformation.md)
## Act V — Make Change Safe and Human (OMF-M17–19)
Plant Director **Elena Petrova (OMF-P07)** requires safe operating limits and rollback. CHRO **Arjun Mehta (OMF-P05)** and shift representative **Nikhil Sen (OMF-P16)** challenge learning that excludes shifts, contractors or people without devices. Customer **Amelia Chen (OMF-P15)** expects certificate correction notifications with accountable owners.
A bounded pilot must test genealogy, laboratory corrections, outage behavior, access controls, drift and human decisions before any controlled expansion.
[Read the Execution theme](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/02-materials/omniforge-materials-ltd/master/theme-e-execution.md)
## Act VI — Prove or Change the Thesis (OMF-M20–22)
Source baseline→Year 3 targets are **OEE68%→83%, downtime 9%→3%, first-pass yield 89%→97%, carbon-intensity index 100→75, recycled content 18%→40%, automation 20%→75%**. None is an achieved result.
The board decides to scale, redesign or stop using observed evidence. The 2030 vision remains aspirational.
[Read the Value theme](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/02-materials/omniforge-materials-ltd/master/theme-f-value.md)
## Meet the Fictional Stakeholders
Ananya Deshpande—CEO; Thomas van Dijk—CFO; Kavita Rao—COO; Sofia de Vries—Digital and Sustainability; Arjun Mehta—CHRO; Musa Dlamini—Mining; Elena Petrova—Cement Plant; Rohan Kulkarni—Quality; Grace Mensah—Supply Chain/Procurement; Li Wei—Commercial; Ingrid Sørensen—Circular Materials; Hassan Al-Farsi—CISO/OT; Priya Nair—Enterprise Architecture; Diego Alvarez—Data/AI; Amelia Chen—Customer; Nikhil Sen—Shift Representative.
[Open persona authority, objections and withheld evidence](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/02-materials/omniforge-materials-ltd/personas/persona-cards.md)
## Practice and Derive
Twelve differentiated simulations cover executive discovery, reliability, investment, workforce, quality certificates, carbon claims, OT architecture, customer escalation, circularity, supply resilience, architecture rehearsal and hypothetical STAR interviews.
Seven scope blueprints cover Workforce/HR, Customer Experience, Finance, Procurement, Supply Chain, Business Transformation and Leadership. External Gamma, Kahoot, Canva, PPT and LMS media remain planned.
[Simulation scripts](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/02-materials/omniforge-materials-ltd/simulations/scenario-scripts.md) · [Stream blueprints](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/02-materials/omniforge-materials-ltd/derived-streams/README.md) · [13 existing HR child-case links](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/02-materials/omniforge-materials-ltd/references/notion-child-cases.md)
## Source and Synchronization Governance
The original research remains the provenance source; GitHub owns the curated case. The exact narrative above the preserved-research boundary maps to a versioned GitHub file. Conflicting edits are held for review. Other canonical files require source-to-narrative reconciliation; arbitrary child pages and attachments are not mirrored.
[Assumptions and unresolved conflicts](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/02-materials/omniforge-materials-ltd/references/source-and-assumptions.md) · [Revision and conflict protocol](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/02-materials/omniforge-materials-ltd/sync/README.md) · [Delivery report](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/02-materials/omniforge-materials-ltd/delivery-report-2026-10-19.md)

# 🌟 GICS02. **OmniForge Materials Ltd. — Digital Transformation Case Study** ## **Company Overview** **OmniForge Materials Ltd.** is a fictional multinational materials company representing the characteristics of leading global producers in metals, mining, cement, chemicals, construction materials, and advanced materials. The company is evolving from asset-intensive, process-driven operations into a digitally enabled, low-carbon materials ecosystem. --- ## **📊 Company Profile**
**Attribute** **Details**
**Founded** 1984 (40+ years of operations)
**Headquarters** Mumbai, India & Rotterdam, Netherlands
**Global Presence** 31 countries across 5 continents
**Annual Revenue** \$42 billion USD
**Employees** 46,000 worldwide
**Market Cap** \$58 billion USD
### **Business Portfolio**
**Business Segment** **Revenue %** **Operations**
**Steel & Alloys** 30% Integrated steel plants, specialty alloys, downstream fabrication
**Cement & Aggregates** 22% 18 cement plants, quarries, ready-mix concrete network
**Industrial Chemicals** 20% Specialty chemicals, coatings, industrial gases, polymer additives
**Mining & Minerals** 16% Iron ore, bauxite, limestone, copper, and rare-earth operations
**Advanced Materials** 12% Battery materials, composites, recycled metals, sustainable packaging
### **Strategic Assets** - **Production Sites:** 54 plants, mills, mines, and processing facilities - **Mining Footprint:** 27 active mines and quarries - **Logistics Network:** 14 ports, 38 distribution hubs, and 8,500 rail and road partners - **R&D Network:** 9 materials-science centers focused on lower-carbon products - **Recycling Capacity:** 4.5 million tonnes of recycled metal and industrial by-products annually --- ## **🎯 Digital Transformation Vision** > *“Creating resilient, circular, and low-carbon materials through intelligent operations, connected value chains, and data-driven innovation.”* ### **Transformation Drivers** 1. **Decarbonization Imperative** — 35% reduction in Scope 1 and 2 emissions by 2032 2. **Operational Reliability** — reduce unplanned downtime across critical plants and mines 3. **Circular Economy Growth** — increase recycled and recovered material content 4. **Supply Chain Resilience** — improve traceability from mine to customer 5. **Customer Innovation** — accelerate development of sustainable, high-performance materials --- # 🏗️ **TOGAF-Aligned Architecture Design** ## **Phase A: Architecture Vision** ### **Business Context & Stakeholders**
**Stakeholder Group** **Key Concerns** **Success Measures**
**Board & Investors** Profitability, risk, ESG performance 14% EBITDA improvement, lower carbon intensity
**Plant & Mine Operations** Safety, availability, productivity 99% critical-asset availability, zero harm
**Customers** Quality, supply certainty, sustainability data 98% on-time delivery, product-carbon transparency
**Regulators & Communities** Environmental compliance, local impact 100% permit compliance and auditable reporting
**Employees & Contractors** Safe work, skills, digital tools 100% critical-safety certification compliance
### **Current-State Challenges** #### **Enterprise Level** - Fragmented planning across mining, production, logistics, sales, and recycling - Inconsistent product, supplier, and asset master data across regions - Limited end-to-end visibility of carbon, quality, and material provenance - Manual environmental, health, safety, and governance reporting #### **Technology Level** - 180+ applications with duplicated functions and point-to-point integrations - Legacy manufacturing execution, laboratory, and maintenance systems - Isolated OT data from PLCs, SCADA, historians, and quality instruments - Cybersecurity exposure created by increasing IT/OT connectivity --- ## **Phase B: Business Architecture** ### **Value Stream Mapping** ```plain text MATERIALS VALUE CHAIN TRANSFORMATION Explore → Extract → Process → Manufacture → Distribute → Recover → Reuse Current State: Siloed planning, manual reconciliations, reactive operations Future State: Connected, traceable, optimized, circular value chain ``` ### **Core Business Capabilities**
**Capability Domain** **Current Maturity** **Target Maturity** **Digital Enablers**
**Asset Management** Level 2 — Reactive Level 4 — Predictive IoT, AI/ML, digital twins
**Production Optimization** Level 2 — Local optimization Level 4 — Autonomous optimization Advanced process control, AI
**Quality Management** Level 2 — Lab-led Level 4 — Real-time quality Machine vision, LIMS integration
**Supply Chain Planning** Level 2 — Spreadsheet driven Level 4 — Resilient and integrated Control tower, optimization models
**Sustainability Reporting** Level 1 — Manual Level 4 — Automated and auditable Carbon data platform, ESG analytics
### **Operating Model Evolution** #### **From: Asset and Function Silos** - Mine, plant, logistics, and commercial teams plan independently - Quality and carbon data reconciled after production - Maintenance decisions driven by failure or fixed schedules #### **To: Integrated Materials Ecosystem** - End-to-end planning from ore body and feedstock to customer demand - Real-time production, quality, energy, and emissions visibility - Predictive maintenance and closed-loop process optimization --- ## **Phase C: Information Systems Architecture** ### **Data Architecture (DAMA-DMBOK Aligned)**
**Data Domain** **Critical Data** **Quality Requirements** **Governance Model**
**Asset Performance** Equipment health, maintenance history, sensor readings 99.5% accuracy, near real time Central asset-data stewardship
**Production & Quality** Throughput, recipe, batch, grade, lab results Traceable, validated, \<5-minute latency Federated plant ownership
**Material Provenance** Mine source, recycled content, certificates of origin End-to-end traceability Supply chain governance
**Customer & Product** Specifications, orders, contracts, product carbon footprint Consistent global master data Commercial data ownership
**ESG Metrics** Emissions, water, waste, safety, biodiversity Auditable and regulatory aligned Enterprise sustainability office
### **Master Data Management Strategy** ```plain text MATERIALS GOLDEN RECORDS Asset 360° → Material 360° → Product 360° → Supplier 360° → Customer 360° Central MDM hub, governed definitions, local stewardship, and real-time synchronization across operational systems. ``` ### **Target Application Landscape**
**Application Layer** **Core Systems** **Architecture Pattern**
**Experience Layer** Customer portal, operator mobile apps, supplier collaboration Micro-frontends, API gateway
**Process Layer** ERP, MES, EAM, LIMS, mine planning, supply-chain planning Domain services, workflow automation
**Integration Layer** iPaaS, event mesh, industrial data hub, B2B gateway API-first, pub/sub, event streaming
**Data Layer** Operational data store, historian, lakehouse, MDM, ESG platform Polyglot persistence and governed data products
--- ## **Phase D: Technology Architecture** ### **Hybrid Industry 4.0 Strategy**
**Workload Type** **Deployment Model** **Rationale**
**Plant and Mine Controls** Edge computing Low latency, operational continuity, safety
**Core ERP and Finance** Private cloud Control, integration, regulatory needs
**Analytics and AI** Public cloud Scalable compute and managed AI services
**Customer and Supplier Services** Public cloud Global availability and digital experience
**Archive and Disaster Recovery** Public cloud cold storage Cost-efficient resilience
### **Technology Standards**
**Technology Stack** **Standard Choice** **Strategic Rationale**
**Industrial Connectivity** OPC UA + MQTT Secure, interoperable OT integration
**Container Platform** Kubernetes / OpenShift Portable application platform
**Data Platform** Snowflake + Databricks Governed analytics and ML at scale
**Integration Platform** SAP Integration Suite / Kafka Enterprise and event-driven connectivity
**Identity & Access** Microsoft Entra ID Centralized zero-trust identity management
--- # 🤖 **AI & Advanced Analytics Architecture** ## **AI Use Case Portfolio** ### **Tier 1: Production-Critical AI**
**Use Case** **Business Value** **Technical Approach** **Implementation Timeline**
**Predictive Maintenance** \$70M annual value Time-series ML, anomaly detection 6 months
**Process Optimization** 4% yield improvement Digital twin, reinforcement learning 12 months
**Quality Prediction** 20% less scrap and rework Multivariate ML, computer vision 8 months
### **Tier 2: Sustainability and Commercial AI**
**Use Case** **Business Value** **Technical Approach** **Implementation Timeline**
**Carbon Footprint Intelligence** Automated product-carbon reporting Emissions engine, data lineage 6 months
**Demand & Inventory Forecasting** 12% inventory reduction Forecasting models, external signals 5 months
**Circularity Optimization** Higher recycled-content utilization Material matching and optimization AI 9 months
### **AI Governance Framework** ```plain text RESPONSIBLE INDUSTRIAL AI Human oversight for safety-critical decisions → explainable models for process and quality recommendations → bias and drift monitoring → data lineage and model audit trails → controlled release through plant safety and change-management gates ``` --- # 🔐 **Security & Risk Architecture** ## **Zero Trust for IT/OT Environments**
**Asset Category** **Security Controls** **Risk Level**
**SCADA and PLC Networks** Segmentation, allowlisting, MFA jump hosts **Critical**
**Production and Quality Systems** Role-based access, immutable audit logs **High**
**Supplier and Logistics Data** API security, partner identity, encryption **High**
**R&D Intellectual Property** DLP, watermarking, least-privilege access **High**
--- # 🌐 **Integration & Interoperability** ## **Event-Driven Material Traceability Model** ```plain text MATERIAL EVENTS Ore / Feedstock Received → Batch Produced → Quality Certified → Shipment Dispatched → Customer Consumed → Material Recovered Event streaming establishes a trusted, traceable record across the value chain. ``` ### **API Strategy**
**API Type** **Use Cases** **Governance**
**Operational APIs** MES, EAM, LIMS, supply-chain orchestration Private, versioned, monitored
**Partner APIs** Logistics, suppliers, recyclers, certification bodies Authenticated, rate-limited
**Customer APIs** Order status, quality certificates, carbon data Consent-based and documented
--- # 📊 **Digital Transformation Roadmap** ## **3-Year Implementation Timeline**
**Phase** **Key Initiatives** **Success Metrics**
**Year 1 — Foundation** Data governance, OT connectivity, critical asset pilots, ESG data baseline 95% master-data quality; 20% assets connected
**Year 2 — Acceleration** Lakehouse rollout, AI at priority plants, supply-chain control tower 10 AI models in production; 10% downtime reduction
**Year 3 — Transformation** Digital twins, circularity platform, autonomous optimization pilots 25% carbon-intensity reduction; 75% processes digitized
--- # 💰 **Business Case & Value Realization** ## **Investment Overview**
**Investment Category** **3-Year Budget** **Key Allocations**
**Digital Operations & OT Modernization** \$230M Connectivity, edge, MES and EAM modernization
**Data & AI Platform** \$125M Lakehouse, AI/ML, governance, digital twins
**Supply Chain & Customer Experience** \$90M Control tower, portals, traceability services
**Cybersecurity** \$55M IT/OT segmentation, monitoring, incident response
**Change & Capability Building** \$40M Workforce upskilling, adoption, operating model
**Total Investment** **\$540M** **Staged deployment over 36 months**
### **Expected Returns** - **Operational Efficiency:** \$190M annual benefit from improved availability, yield, and energy efficiency - **Working Capital:** \$65M annual benefit from inventory and logistics optimization - **Quality and Waste Reduction:** \$55M annual benefit from lower scrap, rework, and claims - **Risk Mitigation:** \$40M annual benefit from improved safety, compliance, and cyber resilience - **Strategic Value:** premium revenue from low-carbon and traceable materials --- # 🎯 **Success Metrics & KPIs**
**Metric** **Baseline** **Year 1 Target** **Year 3 Target**
**Overall Equipment Effectiveness** 68% 74% 83%
**Unplanned Downtime** 9% 6% 3%
**First-Pass Quality Yield** 89% 93% 97%
**Carbon Intensity per Tonne** 100 index 90 index 75 index
**Recycled Material Content** 18% 25% 40%
**Digital Process Automation** 20% 45% 75%
--- # 🚀 **Critical Success Factors** ## **Leadership & Governance** - A Chief Digital and Sustainability Officer jointly accountable for value realization - Cross-functional steering team spanning operations, technology, commercial, finance, safety, and ESG - Plant-level product teams with clear process ownership and safety decision rights ## **Architecture Principles** 1. **Safety by Design** — digital changes never compromise operational safety 2. **Data as a Product** — governed, reusable data assets with accountable owners 3. **Interoperability First** — open industrial standards and API-led integration 4. **Human-Centered Automation** — augment operators and experts before autonomous control 5. **Circular by Default** — embed material traceability, recovery, and carbon transparency in every value stream --- # 🔮 **Future-State Vision** ## **2030: OmniForge Materials as a Circular, Intelligent Materials Leader** - Connected mines, plants, logistics, and customers operating through a unified digital thread - Digital twins optimizing energy, yield, quality, maintenance, and emissions in near real time - Product passports providing customers with verified material origin, recycled content, and carbon footprint - A skilled workforce supported by mobile tools, AI copilots, and standardized safety workflows - A resilient circular-materials ecosystem that turns industrial by-products into high-value inputs --- # 🎉 **Conclusion** **OmniForge Materials Ltd.’s digital transformation** moves the organization from disconnected, asset-heavy operations to a connected and circular materials ecosystem. By combining TOGAF-aligned architecture, DAMA-based data governance, Industry 4.0 technologies, and responsible AI, OmniForge can improve plant performance, customer transparency, sustainability outcomes, and long-term resilience. **Key to success:** disciplined governance, safe IT/OT convergence, trusted data, and a workforce empowered to make better operational decisions. --- ## 14. Aligned business transformation case study blueprint ## Alignment purpose This section refines OmniForge into the same business transformation case study structure used for OmniSpace. It preserves the existing content and adds a publishing-ready storyline for consulting, teaching, and executive communication. ### 14.1 Executive case narrative OmniForge Materials Ltd. is transforming from fragmented, asset-heavy materials operations into a governed, circular, low-carbon, data-led industrial ecosystem. **Core transformation statement:** OmniForge is not only digitizing plants and mines; it is building a repeatable transformation operating model that connects capability architecture, materials traceability, smart operations, ESG data, quality, customer transparency, and measurable value realization. ### 14.2 Business problem statement
**Problem area** **Current challenge** **Transformation need**
Fragmented operations Mines, plants, logistics, quality, recycling, and sales plan independently. Create an end-to-end materials value-chain operating model.
Limited traceability Material origin, quality, recycled content, and carbon footprint are difficult to prove. Build Material 360, Product 360, and carbon-data traceability.
Reactive maintenance Critical equipment reliability depends on fixed schedules and failure response. Use IoT, asset-health analytics, predictive maintenance, and digital twins.
Manual ESG reporting Emissions, water, waste, safety, and biodiversity reporting require reconciliation. Automate ESG data capture, governance, audit trails, and reporting.
IT/OT cybersecurity risk Connected plants, mines, historians, and industrial systems increase exposure. Apply zero trust, segmentation, secure remote access, and OT monitoring.
### 14.3 Target transformation operating model ```plain text Business Outcomes ↓ Capability Architecture — Materials value-chain capabilities ↓ Process Architecture — Mine-to-customer and recover-to-reuse processes ↓ Data Architecture — Asset, material, product, supplier, customer, and ESG golden records ↓ Application Architecture — ERP, MES, EAM, LIMS, planning, customer portals ↓ Integration Architecture — Industrial gateways, APIs, event mesh, B2B integration ↓ Technology Architecture — Edge, hybrid cloud, AI/ML, digital twins ↓ Security, Sustainability, Adoption, and Value Realization ``` **Operating rule:** Every workstream must connect to a business capability, process owner, data domain, application owner, integration dependency, safety control, ESG metric, adoption plan, and business value KPI. ### 14.4 Workstream alignment map
**Workstream** **Business outcome** **Architecture / process focus** **Delivery and adoption focus**
Smart operations Higher uptime, yield, and energy efficiency. Asset 360, MES, EAM, historian, digital twin. IoT connectivity, predictive alerts, operator dashboards.
Material traceability Verified quality, origin, recycled content, and carbon data. Material 360, product passport, LIMS, ESG lineage. Event streaming, certificates, customer portal integration.
Circular value chain Higher recycled-content utilization and lower waste. Recover-to-reuse process, supplier and recycler data. Circularity platform, material matching, partner APIs.
IT/OT resilience Safe, secure, reliable connected operations. Network segmentation, identity, risk classification. OT monitoring, secure remote access, incident response drills.
### 14.5 Case study structure for publishing 1. **Situation** - OmniForge operates plants, mines, logistics networks, recycling flows, and advanced-materials R&D across global markets. 2. **Challenge** - The company must improve reliability, carbon transparency, traceability, quality, circularity, and IT/OT resilience. 3. **Transformation approach** - Use TOGAF-aligned architecture, DAMA data governance, Industry 4.0, edge computing, AI, digital twins, and ESG traceability. 4. **Execution model** - Mobilize around safety, connect critical assets, govern master data, modernize applications, scale AI, and institutionalize value tracking. 5. **Value realization** - Measure OEE, downtime, first-pass quality, carbon intensity, recycled content, automation, and customer transparency. 6. **Long-term capability** - Establish a repeatable materials transformation model from extraction to recovery and reuse. ### 14.6 Alignment rules - **Safety first:** Digital change must never compromise operational safety. - **Capability first:** Every initiative must map to a clear materials business capability. - **Traceability by design:** Material, product, quality, and carbon data must be auditable. - **IT/OT secure by default:** Segmentation, identity, monitoring, and response are mandatory. - **Circularity embedded:** Recovery and reuse must be designed into the operating model. - **Value after go-live:** Deployment starts the benefit-realization cycle. ### 14.7 Final aligned positioning ## Aligned case study positioning OmniForge Materials Ltd. demonstrates how a materials enterprise can connect smart operations, material traceability, ESG data, circularity, IT/OT security, and value realization into one integrated transformation operating model. #
